 Benda Capra 700 revealed at Eicma! Chinese cruiser brand's first adventure bike is a 72bhp V-twin
 By Ben Clarke

 Published: 03 November 2026

 1 of 7 
 Chinese brand Benda have used Eicma to reveal their first adventure bike , the Capra 700 – a 692cc V-twin with a 21in front wheel that takes the cruiser specialists into entirely new territory.
 Benda arrived in the UK in 2025 through importer MotoGB with a trio of cruisers – the 500cc Chinchilla and NapoleonBob and the £8999 LFC700 , whose 676cc inline-four and 310-section rear tyre earned it three stars from MCN.
 A 950cc V4 Dark Flag cruiser followed, which we’re yet to ride. The Capra is their first attempt at anything with long-travel suspension, and Benda say it was developed specifically for Europe, with their EU design team working alongside engineers in Hangzhou.
 Named after the Latin genus for the ibex (apparently), the Capra 700 is pitched as a road-focused adventure bike rather than a hardcore off-roader, though the chassis spec is more serious than that suggests.
 A steel trellis frame and aluminium swingarm carry an adjustable upside-down fork with 230mm of travel and a monoshock with piggyback reservoir giving 220mm at the rear, both adjustable for compression and rebound. Wheels are 21in front and 18in rear, shod with 90/90 and 150/70 tyres ( Pirelli Scorpion Rally STR s in the images).
 The engine is a liquid-cooled 65-degree V-twin of 691.66cc – a configuration new to Benda’s range – producing 72bhp at 9000rpm and 50lb.ft at 6500rpm, with ride-by-wire, a six-speed gearbox and a slipper clutch. Brakes are a single front disc with a four-piston radial Brembo caliper and a single-piston Brembo rear, with two-channel ABS and traction control.
 The styling is rugged, with exposed mechanical parts and a high-mounted twin exhaust, a distinctive DRL signature with integrated fog lights, crash bars designed in from the start and a utility rack above the tank with slots for mounting equipment. A vertical TFT dash and a USB-A socket complete the kit.
 Vital statistics are an 850mm seat, 220kg kerb weight, 18-litre tank and 1599mm wheelbase, with overall dimensions of 2306mm long, 1050mm wide and 1397mm tall.
 “Entering the adventure motorcycle segment represents a significant step in expanding our portfolio and reaching new riders, while bringing Benda’s design philosophy to a new category,” said George Schelfaut, transportation designer at Benda Motor Europe. “We’re proud to introduce the Capra 700 and look forward to sharing more details soon.”
 No price or on-sale date has been given, and UK availability has yet to be confirmed.
 The MCN take
 Benda have become known for doing things nobody else would – a four-cylinder cruiser with a 310-section tyre or a 250cc boxer hybrid concept, for example – so a relatively conventional middleweight adventure bike is almost a surprise.
 But the 700-class adventure market has enormous sales volume potential, and a 72bhp V-twin with a 21in front, 230mm of travel and adjustable suspension at both ends is a credible spec.

 Ben Clarke 
 Deputy Head of Digital (Motorcycling) 
 Ben Clarke began riding (legally) at 21-years-old when he passed his direct access one month before shipping his Yamaha XT660 R to Miami and embarking on a 13,500-mile tour of the USA and Central America. He's worked at MCN for the last six years, riding everything from super nakeds and superbikes to small-capacity electrics and scooters across several continents. In more recent years, he's worked closely with the bike kit team to bring you all the latest news and reviews about the bike-related products we all use every day.
